text:
alex kim: kicking off staged rollout for service-api v2.4.1 -> starting canary at 15% in us-west-2. change window ends 20:00 PST. tagging @sre-oncall for go/no-go.
maria gonzalez: got it. release notes link: https://internal.redwood/release/v2.4.1 - includes kv cache change + quantization tweak. any pinned versions for fallback?
deploy-bot: [deploy] initiating canary: service-api v2.4.1 -> 15% traffic (us-west-2). canary id=cb-1765439876. logs:
```
[1765439876] route-shift: 15% -> started
[1765439876] instances: 8 new pods in pool
[1765439877] health: 8/8 OK
```
leo wu: watching latency + 90p tail. will share Grafana snapshot in 2m.
sre-oncall: +1 watching error budget and 95p latency. set threshold: error rate > 1.5% OR tail latency +30% -> hold.
maria gonzalez: note: we pinned model weights to v2.4-quant-a for the canary; fallback is v2.3.9 (pinned by product) if we need rollback.
leo wu: grafana snapshot: https://grafana/shot/AA12 - seeing KV cache evictions spike on canary traffic. baseline evictions 120/s -> canary 980/s :warning:
```
metric: kv_cache_evictions/s
baseline: 120
canary: 980
threshold: 500
```
alex kim: hmm, that's > threshold. are we seeing increased 5xx?
sre-oncall: yes — 5xx increased from 0.4% to 2.9% in the canary cohort. pausing rollout and holding at 15%. marking incident. :rotating_light:
deploy-bot: [deploy] pausing canary cb-1765439876 -> traffic frozen at 15%. taking health snapshot.
product-ops: noting in release tracker: hold at 15% due to kv cache thrash. will update customer-facing comms if we escalate.
maria gonzalez: quick triage: the quant change altered KV key alignment; possible cache miss storm. rolling back the quant patch on canary replicas could be faster than full rollback. thoughts?
sre-oncall: prefer rollback to stable (v2.3.9) for now until we confirm fix. reduced blast radius. we can re-run an A/B after fix.
leo wu: agree — rollback path looks simple: deploy-bot rollback to v2.3.9 for canary id cb-1765439876. need ops approval to run.
alex kim: ops approved in thread. @deploy-bot run rollback to v2.3.9 for canary only. keep logs verbose.
deploy-bot: [deploy] rolling back canary cb-1765439876 -> target version v2.3.9. commands: `/deploy rollback cb-1765439876 --version v2.3.9 --cohort canary`
```
[1765439901] rollback start
[1765439912] drain 15% traffic -> switch
[1765439930] health checks: 8/8 OK
[1765439945] rollback complete, canary at v2.3.9, traffic stable
```
leo wu: post-rollback checks look good. kv evictions back to ~130/s, 5xx down to 0.6%.
sre-oncall: closing hold. marking rollback executed. recommend reverting quant change in next patch and adding unit/integration test for kv key alignment.
maria gonzalez: I'll open a PR to revert quant tweak and add tests. tagging @product-ops to update release notes and change window: we should reopen tomorrow 09:00 PT for a reattempt after fixes.
product-ops: noted — update scheduled. customer-facing note draft will say: "minor canary hold for internal rollback, no customer impact observed beyond elevated internal 5xx; monitoring continues."
alex kim: thanks everyone. file incident and include canary id cb-1765439876. will re-open when PR merges and tests pass. :thumbsup:
